headline: Profit jumps, guidance raised as debt climbs on Masimo deal
summary_short: Danaher's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 5.5% y/y to $6,265M and GAAP net earnings jumped 59.7% y/y to $870M ($1.23 diluted EPS), while adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted EPS grew a smaller 8.0% to $1.94 once acquisition-related charges are excluded.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5.5% y/y to $6,265M as core sales rose 3.0% (4.5% ex-respiratory testing); Life Sciences had its strongest quarter in years, bioprocessing lagged on project timing despite mid-teens order growth. GAAP net earnings rose 59.7% y/y to $870M since 2025 had $0.60/share of trade-name/facility impairments; adjusted diluted EPS grew a smaller 8.0% to $1.94 once $0.65/share of acquisition-intangible amortization and $0.15/share of Masimo deal costs are excluded. Danaher closed Masimo earlier than expected in the quarter, funding a $10.1B investing outflow with $7.3B of new financing; long-term debt rose 43.7% q/q to $26,558M and cash fell 23.7% q/q to $4,348M. Company raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.45-$8.60 from $8.35-$8.55 and guides FY2026 core revenue growth to 3.0-4.0%.

drivers.explanation: Total sales grew 5.5% y/y on broad-based growth; core sales (non-GAAP) rose 3.0%, or 4.5% excluding respiratory testing, since respiratory-test demand is normalizing off elevated 2025 levels.

GAAP diluted EPS more than doubled y/y mainly because 2025 included a one-time $0.60/share trade-name and facility impairment that didn't recur; adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS rose a smaller 8.0% once acquisition-intangible amortization and Masimo deal costs are excluded.

Life Sciences had its strongest quarter in years and bioprocessing orders grew mid-teens, though bioprocessing revenue was held back by customer project timing; management cites disciplined execution and the earlier-than-expected Masimo close for the raised full-year EPS guidance.
Debt rose q/q alongside a $10.1B investing outflow and $7.3B financing inflow in the quarter, consistent with funding the Masimo acquisition that closed during Q2.
Cash fell q/q as the $10.1B Masimo-related investing outflow outpaced $7.3B of financing inflows and $1.5B of operating cash flow.
